findings.message: `configure()` sets module globals (ROOT, STATE, CONFIG, EXEC, GIT, ENV), and nothing resets them. The new tests in tests/test_watch.py call `main([... 'snapshot'])`, which leaves STATE pointing at that test's `custom-state` dir. The suite runs with `-n auto`, so any later test on the same worker that only monkeypatches ROOT reads the wrong directory. That includes `test_queue_projection_and_fallback` (`state_dir()/queue.json`) and `test_recent_steps_merges_engine_and_stage_events` (`text_snapshot()`). The tests now depend on order.
findings.paved_road: Pass the configured context (root, state dir, config path, exec, git, env) into `snapshot()` and `text_snapshot()` as an explicit object, or have the tests restore every global with monkeypatch. No call should leave process-wide state behind.

findings.message: `state_dir()` falls back to `ROOT / "state"` when the module is not configured. This is an invented default that matches neither the old config-reading behavior nor the engine's `.chupa/state`. The existing tests now pass only because their tmp dirs happen to use `state`, and the `config.yaml` they write is dead.
findings.paved_road: Require a configured state dir (no fallback), and make the existing tests supply it explicitly instead of relying on the default.

findings.message: `./dev.py watch` now goes through `chupa()` -> `run()` -> `subprocess.run` without the `KeyboardInterrupt` handler the old code had. Ctrl-C reaches dev.py's process group too, so stopping the live view now prints a traceback instead of exiting normally. The child exiting 0 does not prevent dev.py's own KeyboardInterrupt.
findings.paved_road: Keep the `try/except KeyboardInterrupt: pass` around the `chupa("watch", ...)` call in dev.py.
